title: How the internet began
examples: What was the main purpose of ARPANET?
How is the World Wide Web different from the Internet?
Who is credited with creating the World Wide Web?

explain.say: Today we will learn about the start of the internet. It was a big journey over time.

items: World Wide Web: Information sharing system

explain.say: The first step was ARPANET. This was developed by the US Department of Defense. It allowed computers to communicate using packets.
Next came the World Wide Web. This system made information easily accessible to everyone. It used web browsers and hyperlinks.
Tim Berners-Lee is the key person here. He invented the World Wide Web while working at CERN. He created HTML and HTTP.
In real life, think about sending a digital document. You use the World Wide Web to view it. The Internet is the wires connecting you to the server.
A common mistake is confusing the Web and the Internet. Remember the Web is an application that runs on the larger Internet structure.

items: The World Wide Web is the software/service.
One needs the other to function fully.

draw.text: Web is part of the Internet

faq.q: What was ARPANET originally designed for?
faq.a: It was initially developed to allow different types of computers to communicate reliably. It was part of research funding from the US Department of Defense.
asks: What was the purpose of ARPANET?

faq.q: Is the World Wide Web the same thing as the Internet?
faq.a: No, they are not the same thing. The Internet is the massive network of cables and computers, while the Web is one service running on top of it.
asks: Are the Web and the Internet interchangeable terms?
What is the difference between WWW and the Internet?

faq.q: Who invented the World Wide Web?
faq.a: Tim Berners-Lee is credited with inventing the World Wide Web. He developed the core technologies like HTML and HTTP.
asks: Who created the web pages we use?
Can you name the inventor of the WWW?

faq.a: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language. It is the standard language used to create web pages.
asks: What does the 'L' in HTML mean?

faq.q: Did the World Wide Web appear all at once?
faq.a: No, it developed over time. ARPANET was the precursor, and then Berners-Lee built the specific structure we now call the Web.
asks: Was the Web invented in one day?
What came before the World Wide Web?

facts: ARPANET was a precursor network developed in the late 1960s.
Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989.
The Web relies on protocols like HTTP for communication.
The Internet is the physical infrastructure connecting computers globally.

quiz.say: The early network that allowed computers to communicate using packets was called:
quiz.why: ARPANET was the specific early network developed for this purpose.

wrong.1: The Web came later and is an information system, not the original network.
wrong.2: HTTP is a protocol used by the Web, not the name of the original network.
wrong.3: CERN was the place where the Web was developed, not the network itself.

quiz.say: Which individual is credited with inventing the World Wide Web?
quiz.why: He is the scientist who developed the core standards for the Web.

wrong.0: NASA funded early computing, but they did not invent the World Wide Web.
wrong.2: Vint Cerf is known for co-developing TCP/IP, which is foundational, but not the Web itself.
wrong.3: Robert Kahn was instrumental in the early networking concepts, but not the Web's invention.

quiz.say: The World Wide Web uses which language to structure its pages?
quiz.why: HTML is the specific markup language used to write the content of web pages.

wrong.1: HTTP is the transfer rule, not the language used to write the page content.
wrong.2: TCP/IP are the underlying rules that allow data to travel across the network.
wrong.3: ARPANET was the name of the early network, not a programming language.
